top_story: US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz on 31 August broke a month-long pause and drew Iranian retaliation against US bases in Jordan and the UAE, reopening a direct military cycle around one of the world’s most vulnerable energy corridors. That exchange escalated after Washington said Iran was preparing to deploy new mines, and Trump’s threat of further action kept confrontation ahead of diplomacy even as Tehran signaled it would reciprocate if the US honored the June interim deal. The 1 September attack on two Saudi oil tankers in the strait shows how quickly state-to-state escalation is spilling into commercial shipping and broader market insecurity. The immediate risk is not only a wider US-Iran clash, but a regional crisis that pushes Gulf states deeper into the line of fire and raises economic pressure far beyond the battlefield.
